author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260511T032340Z-4081086
text:
Spec ambiguity in the RevocationCache trait shape — the bead's API sketch and the parent acceptance criterion don't line up cleanly. Need a decision before implementation.

The bead sketches:

    trait RevocationCache {
        fn get_crl(&self, key: &CrlCacheKey) -> Option<Arc<Vec<u8>>>;
        fn put_crl(&self, key: CrlCacheKey, bytes: Vec<u8>);
        ...
    }
    struct CrlCacheKey { issuer_dn_der: Vec<u8>, crl_number: Option<Vec<u8>> }

But CrlCacheKey.crl_number is only known **after** the wrapper has fetched and parsed the CRL — so the natural CachedHttpCrlFetcher::check_revocation lookup before fetching can't construct a full CrlCacheKey. The bead hedges "If absent, key by issuer DN only and treat the cache as last-seen" which suggests using crl_number=None as the lookup key. This works but the resulting algorithm stores under (issuer, None) before any CRL is seen, then under (issuer, Some(N)) after — which means either redundant writes or a hidden second lookup channel.

Three plausible shapes I considered:

A. **Cache by issuer DN; store CRLNumber as metadata.**
   trait method takes &[u8] issuer DN. Cleaner; diverges from the bead's literal API sketch.
   - lookup: get_crl(issuer_dn_der) -> Option<Arc<CachedCrl>>
   - put: put_crl(CachedCrl { issuer_dn_der, crl_number, bytes, expires_at })

B. **Cache by (issuer_dn_der, crl_number), with a separate scan-by-issuer method.**
   Matches the bead's CrlCacheKey but adds a second trait method not in the sketch.
   - lookup-targeted: get_crl(&CrlCacheKey) — useful when consumer knows the CRLNumber it wants
   - lookup-scan: get_crl_any_for_issuer(issuer_dn_der, now_unix) — used by the wrapper before fetching
   - put: put_crl(key, bytes, expires_at)

C. **The wrapper stores under (issuer, None) AND (issuer, Some(N)).**
   Literal-bead-API but doubles every write and the (issuer, None) entry is a hidden alias.
   - lookup: get_crl(&CrlCacheKey { issuer, crl_number: None }) before fetch
   - put: put_crl twice — once with the actual key, once with crl_number: None as last-seen.

My recommendation is **Shape A** — it's the cleanest fit for what the wrapper actually needs (it doesn't know CRLNumber until after the fetch, so the read-side key doesn't benefit from including it). CRLNumber is genuinely useful metadata for the consumer to compare staleness, but it's metadata, not part of the lookup key. Shape A also generalises naturally to OCSP where the cert serial + issuer key hash + responder URL ARE all known a-priori, so OcspCacheKey can stay as the literal bead sketch.

Asking for the human decision because picking B or C anyway would technically satisfy the bead's literal API sketch but lock the trait surface in a way I'd rather not commit to without confirmation. The trait is the public surface and version-binding once pkix-revocation-http is published.

Releasing the claim — bd-spin will re-surface this when human decides.
